profile.campus: Silicon Valley (San Jose/Santa Clara), California (Equinix's founding market, Great Oaks/Corvin/Duane campuses)
profile.address: 2970 Corvin Drive, Pod C, Santa Clara, CA 95051
profile.reading:
This building is Equinix's SV15 facility, part of Equinix's Silicon Valley data center network in the San Jose/Santa Clara area. Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers, on the idea of building a neutral place where competing internet networks could physically connect and exchange traffic, a model that let the company grow through network effects as more networks joined; Equinix converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Silicon Valley, where Equinix is still headquartered today in nearby Redwood City, was the company's founding market, and its San Jose facilities on Great Oaks Boulevard and its Santa Clara facilities on Corvin Drive and Duane Avenue grew into one of the densest interconnection hubs in Equinix's global network as the company expanded internationally, entering Asia-Pacific in 2002, Europe via the IXEurope acquisition in 2007, Latin America in 2011, and the Middle East in 2013, and opening its 50th global data center in London by 2010 around the time it acquired Switch and Data Facilities Company. Equinix's own published specifications for the flagship SV1 building on this campus describe an 82,850-square-foot, single-story, steel-frame facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 2kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, and generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load; Equinix markets the Great Oaks campus for its direct connections to major networks and tier-1 cloud service providers. Equinix's website did not disclose this specific building's own square footage or power capacity separately from the SV1 figure cited as representative of the broader campus.

Pacific Gas and Electric, the regional utility serving most of Silicon Valley, and Silicon Valley Power, Santa Clara's municipal utility, have both cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in their own capacity planning, a dynamic distinct from the newer data center markets elsewhere in the country given how built-out and power-constrained the Bay Area grid already is after decades of continuous data center development since Equinix's own 1998 founding in the area.

reading.body:
Equinix SV15 is a 28,514 square foot retail colocation facility in Santa Clara, California with N+1 redundancy for both power and cooling, but no megawatt capacity is published on the operator's specification page. The facility is part of Equinix's Silicon Valley metro footprint of 12 buildings, which the operator describes as the region's largest retail colocation asset and serves over 10,500 customers across enterprises and network service providers.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities, of which 11 publish power capacity totaling 365 MW. SV15 does not appear among those 11 published figures, so its actual power draw cannot be assessed against the state total or ranked by consumption. Without published megawatt specifications for this facility, it cannot be evaluated for its contribution to California's data center power demand or its significance to AI infrastructure scaling in the state.

The building's specification emphasizes redundancy architecture rather than absolute capacity, which is typical for retail colocation marketing but leaves the critical constraint unmeasured. To assess whether SV15 matters to AI infrastructure, a reader would need to determine its actual power allocation and cooling capacity through means beyond the published specifications provided here.
